feed.title: NCM-MLX research updates
feed.subtitle: Software and working-paper releases for an independent MLX implementation of Next-Concept Modeling.

entry.title: Software 0.2.0: released NCM checkpoints in MLX
entry.summary: Runs HazyResearch's released TinyStories and Sudoku checkpoints natively in MLX on the Apple GPU, inference only. Per-level logits match upstream PyTorch to 3.2e-10 (TinyStories) and 1.2e-13 (Sudoku) in exact fp64; greedy generation is identical. Greedy Sudoku solve rates on all 2,000 boards per difficulty: 99.40 / 96.30 / 86.20% (paper: 99.5 / 96.5 / 86.1%). LM1B, OpenWebText, WMT14 and XSum are not converted.

entry.title: Software 0.1.1: first PyPI release
entry.summary: Packaging and metadata release: pip install ncm-mlx on Apple Silicon or ncm-mlx[cuda] on Linux NVIDIA, author ORCID in citation metadata and a refreshed README. Model code and recorded results are unchanged from 0.1.0. The project's own trained Sudoku and TinyWorld weights are published separately on Hugging Face.

entry.title: Working paper v0.11: two-seed Sudoku assessment and planned text research
entry.summary: Completed E20 records 97.25 / 79.60 / 33.25% easy/medium/hard solving, compared with seed 0's 98.10 / 83.40 / 40.30% at equal generator exposure. A partial small-model success with a substantial hard-board deficit, two-seed uncertainty and explicit historical audit limits. Controlled text generation is the next research direction, not a validated capability. Unreviewed working paper.

entry.title: Working paper v0.10: completed E18 and E19 results
entry.summary: Completed E18, E19 pilot and E19-funded results. The independent MLX implementation solves 98.10 / 83.40 / 40.30% of easy/medium/hard boards. Easy accuracy is within 1.40 points of Original NCM (Kumbong et al.) with a 3.95x smaller generator; medium/hard gaps, additional codec and unmatched budgets remain explicit. Includes checkpoint provenance, uncertainty and A40 timings. Unreviewed working paper.

entry.title: Working paper v0.9
entry.summary: Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation on a Laptop: A Native MLX Study of Next-Concept Modeling. Version 0.9 corrects reproduction instructions and experimental settings and adds an AI-assistance disclosure. This working paper is not peer reviewed. The method is due to Kumbong et al.; the independent MLX experiments cover synthetic text and Sudoku, with explicit model-size and training-budget qualifications.

entry.title: Software v0.1.0
entry.summary: Initial MIT-licensed research source release: multiscale residual VQ codec, parallel coarse-to-fine generator, from-scratch training, autoregressive baseline and synchronized benchmarks. Verified execution on Apple Silicon Metal and selected Linux NVIDIA CUDA GPUs. Experimental TinyWorld and Sudoku software; no model weights, general-text validation or upstream checkpoint compatibility are included.
